entities.summary: The Prehistoric era, spanning approximately 70000 BCE to 3000 BCE, represents the vast epoch before the advent of written records, fundamentally shaping human biological and cultural development. This immense timeframe, classified as division 910 in the Annals of the World Dewey-style system, witnessed the emergence of anatomically modern humans, the global dispersal of populations, and the foundational innovations that underpin all subsequent civilizations. It encompasses the Paleolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic periods, each marked by distinct technological and social transformations, from nomadic hunter-gatherer societies to the first settled agricultural communities.
